claims.statement: cmd/harness/main.go is a thin shell over harnessapp.RunRootCommand, and cmd/harness/harnessapp is the module's only composition root: the dependency ratchet's isCompositionRoot admits exactly this path for concrete-adapter imports, and wiring happens explicitly via wireDependencies() under sync.Once (mirrored by harnessapp's TestMain) rather than via init() side effects.

Per-command flag/parse/render/dispatch lives in cmd/harness/*cli packages (issueopscli, mcpcli, daemoncli, policycli, installcli, workercli, gatescli, channelcli, loopcli, and others); the rootcmd.Command runner map in harnessapp owns only dispatch plus exit-code policy (policy/guard denial exits 3, gates usage error exits 2), and CLI packages must not re-own host policy or domain judgment.

internal/domain/cli owns the canonical top-level command catalog (Commands()) and the human usage text (Usage(version)); harnessapp only renders it, the issueops usage lines are composed solely from issueOpsUsageCatalog so a command cannot be hand-written in two places, and the contractgolden suite pins the rendered usage text against a golden file.

internal/domain/mcp owns the MCP tool vocabulary: both the advertised tools/list (AdvertisedTools) and the name-to-handler routing table (DispatchMap) derive from the single ordered catalogSections() slice, so adding a tool to one catalog function makes it advertised and routable; cmd/harness/mcpcli owns only the stdio/JSON-RPC transport and handler wiring.

internal/adapter/mcp is restricted to a capture-only conformance probe that advertises one tool per episode and never registers or invokes production catalog handlers; schema semantics and gate decisions live in internal/contract/toolconformance and internal/domain/toolconformance, and fixture I/O plus replay live in internal/adapter/toolconformance.

cmd/harness/daemoncli owns the daemon lifecycle and the MCP stdio proxy, which fails explicitly on daemon restart with JSON-RPC error -32002 (daemon_generation_changed) instead of silently retrying; the worker plane is one-shot lifecycle jobs plus a policy-gated read-only executor, and there is no long-resident job daemon — the daemon backs only the MCP proxy.

The command/tool surface is mechanically pinned: cmd/harness/contractgolden goldens the CLI usage text and MCP tool/resource catalogs under cmd/harness/testdata, and the harnessapp response-contract suite runs the full CLI+MCP surface under a temporary state dir and goldens the combined snapshot, so CLI/MCP response contracts cannot drift silently.

The layer contract is: internal/contract holds versioned DTOs and error vocabulary (no judgment logic or I/O); internal/domain holds pure rules/reducers/classifiers (no adapter/cmd imports, no filesystem/process/DB I/O, clock injected with internal/domain/auditid as the recorded exception); internal/application composes contract/domain/port and never imports concrete adapters or cmd; internal/port imports only contract; adapter/inbound maps requests to application calls and must not import outbound adapters; adapter/outbound implements state/SQL/webfetch I/O without duplicating transport policy or domain judgment.

Contracts pin durable bytes without implementation knowledge: internal/contract/issueopslease/stable_v1.go re-declares the persisted v1 record shape with no implementation types so canonicalization cannot drift; the ownership rules fail any contract-to-implementation edge, and per-vertical rules additionally forbid the lease contract from importing production IssueOps code.

Domain packages carry no I/O: the ratchet bans domain imports of application, adapter, cmd, contract, os, os/exec, net, net/http, database/sql, syscall, and anything sqlite; clocks are injected by default with internal/domain/auditid's timestamped audit IDs as the documented exception, and internal/domain/pioneerskill pins the 12 canonical pioneer skill names.

Application use cases may not import concrete adapters, cmd, or transport stdlib — application_must_not_import_implementation fires even on path/filepath — and the ownership lens additionally rejects application-to-adapter/cmd edges, so use cases declare their needs as narrow local port interfaces instead.

internal/port speaks contract vocabulary only (port->contract and port->port allowed; port_must_not_import_internal blocks domain/application/adapter/cmd) and holds deliberately narrow surfaces: TransactionalRecordStore/RecordCASStore span+CAS operations, IssueProvider request/result DTOs, port.HostInstaller, IssueOps owner-model defaults, and issueopsbasesync restricted by test to the types Request, Receipt, and Inspector plus a single context import.

The only non-composition-root concrete-adapter edges are the shared storage primitives: internal/adapter/outbound/sqlstore may be imported by any outbound/* adapter and by internal/adapter/issueops, and outbound/issueopsrecord (the shared IssueOps record codec/lock primitive) only by outbound/issueops* adapters; cmd, inbound, and domain reaching the engine directly fail, duplicate per-vertical record codecs are rejected, and the ratchet's isSameCapabilityAdapter treats same-capability subpackage edges as implementation cleanup rather than coupling.

internal/adapter/outbound/sqlstore is the shared SQLite engine for all harness state: each store root owns harness.db (records as bucket/id/data-JSON rows) and harness.lock.db (cross-process locks held as BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions for the duration of a read-modify-write span, so locks die with the holder process); handles are cached per absolute directory, nested spans are rejected, and it satisfies both port.TransactionalRecordStore and the port/state store interfaces.

Host installation follows the port/adapter shape: install.InstallNative is the host-neutral engine that normalizes inputs and skill lists and delegates to port.HostInstaller implementations; harnessapp passes exactly the three first-party installers (codex, claude, omo), and each installer (e.g. the Codex adapter) writes only its own user-level skill symlinks, MCP registration, and SessionStart hook config plus configs/ templates.

Adding a host means implementing port.HostInstaller and adding composition-root wiring only — host domain/application policy must not be duplicated, and the install contract matrix test detects surface drift across hosts.

Because cross-capability adapter imports are banned at zero tolerance, consumer packages declare needs as package-level function variables in dedicated adapter_dependencies.go files (issueops's GitCmd/GitCmdRaw/GitOut, gatesgate's DiscoverGateFiles/CheckGateLedger) and harnessapp wiring functions assign implementations; there are no default implementations — an un-injected dependency must surface as a structured fail-closed error — and tests inject the same concrete implementations that production wires.

internal/architecture is a test-only fitness boundary: it loads direct production import edges via go list -json ./..., enforces the unconditional layer rules and the zero legacy-adapter baseline over the whole graph, and additionally guards against orphaned packages (TestProductionPackagesHaveImporters, motivated by a wiring deletion that silently disabled a PR-target guard), stale canonical documentation paths, and coding-convention drift such as errors.As instead of errors.AsType.

A capability vertical packages one capability across five layers — contract/<cap> for persisted/request shapes, domain/<cap> for pure decisions and deny codes, application/<cap> for orchestration over narrow ports.go interfaces, adapter/inbound/<cap> for transport mapping, adapter/outbound/<cap> for persistence and side effects — with cmd/harness/harnessapp as the only place they are wired; fitness tests require all five layers for migrated capabilities and forbid them from importing the legacy internal/adapter/issueops root, and the issueopslease execution claim is the worked example: harnessapp opens sqlstore, builds the outbound preflight/repository/clock/process-inspector, composes ClaimService, and hands it to the inbound handler, whose errors map back through domain deny codes rather than string matching.

internal/application/issueopslease declares only the operations it uses (ClaimRepository, ClaimContextPreflight, Clock, ProcessInspector, Reseed/Resume fences and repositories) in ports.go, and its ClaimService composes preflight -> actor resolution -> repository claim, with the outbound claim preflight validating sealed issue-body and context-packet SHA-256 digests against the stored record and the live remote issue snapshot.

issueopspublication (remote PR/MR creation and recovery) demonstrates the vertical with a fail-closed domain decision: the application declares narrow Repository/Provider/Verifier intent-lifecycle interfaces, the domain's DecideReconcile adopts exactly one verified candidate, preserves on multiple candidates/non-authoritative zero/unknown invocation/exhausted retries (only a proven not_invoked outcome is retryable), and harnessapp composes the outbound repository/gateway/verifier into CreateService/ReconcileService wrapped by inbound handlers so CLI create and CLI/MCP reconcile share one request-scoped handler pair with no legacy fallback.

internal/adapter/issueops remains the record-backed IssueOps capability adapter (with same-capability subpackages such as loopgate and gatesgate) and is one of the two allowed direct users of the sqlstore engine; internal/adapter/provider resolves github/gitlab provider implementations behind port.IssueProvider so no core package imports concrete providers.

configs/ holds host configuration templates (configs/codex/mcp.config.toml and hooks.json written by the Codex installer, the claude and omo analogs) plus configs/upstream.json, an optional post-activation Claude plugin/skill provisioning catalog whose network or CLI failures must never fail the native install or become a core dependency; the repo-root .mcp.json is dogfood-only project-local MCP configuration that default installs must not copy into target repositories.

skills/ is the single host-neutral source of truth for 34 shared skills (12 pioneer-namesake plus 22 operational); default installs symlink the same sources into each host's user skill directory rather than copying, host-specific skill copies are forbidden drift, and internal/domain/pioneerskill enforces the pioneer catalog in code.

.agent-harness/ is the git-tracked agent knowledge base and lifecycle layout: canonical architecture/conventions docs (kept aligned with layer paths by the documentation test), ADRs, cautions, evidence, and per-issue artifact folders .agent-harness/issues/<issue-number>/ whose gates.md is the canonical task-gate ledger that PR readiness reads (with duplicate canonical-plus-legacy ledgers failing closed as duplicate_issue_artifact:<n>); project bootstrap manages only its marker block inside a target repo's AGENTS.md.

scripts/install-native.sh builds bin/agent-harness and drives agent-harness install as a staged activation transaction (begin/commit/abort with SHA-256-verified binary candidates and recovery via a pending transition on abort) while forwarding install flags such as --project-local and --dry-run; the remaining scripts validate skill contracts and shell-skill behavior, and install/update paths stay independently runnable without provisioning external tools on core's behalf.

testdata/ holds cross-cutting fixtures (issueops/fixtures, webfetch/live, pioneer-holdouts inputs) and cmd/harness/testdata the contract goldens; internal/testsupport provides shared stdout/stderr capture helpers; internal/holdoutdeleak mechanically guarantees the committed pioneer-holdout fixtures contain inputs only and never recorded answers; and intentionally unimported test-support packages are admitted only through orphanPackageAllowlist with a written reason.

The extension points mirror the map: a new command is a cmd/harness/<cli> package plus a harnessapp facade and a canonical description in internal/domain/cli (the usage golden forces agreement); a new MCP tool is one catalogSections() entry in internal/domain/mcp (adding it to a section makes it both advertised and routable); and a new IssueOps capability is the five vertical layers plus a <cap>_vertical_test.go in internal/architecture, with shared record access via outbound/issueopsrecord.
